free_tier.stated: Unlimited private Git repositories free per organization; each repository may be up to 250 GB; storage is NOT a billed meter - the Azure DevOps free tier bills only users, parallel jobs and Artifacts storage. Git LFS is free and does not count toward the 5 GB push limit.

egress.terms: Unmetered. Clone/fetch over HTTPS from dev.azure.com has no egress meter - the billing FAQ enumerates every chargeable meter (extra Basic users, Basic+Test Plans, parallel jobs, Artifacts >2 GB, GHAS) and data transfer is not among them.

record.tooling: Plain git / git-lfs; Azure DevOps REST API for repository + item download (GET /_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items?path=); rclone has no ADO Repos backend, so use git or the REST item API
record.chaining: Unlimited repos x 250 GB each within one org; each org holds up to 1,000 projects; orgs are free and you may hold many. 250 GB x N repos x M orgs. The 2026 sprint-273 change removed the Git object-count limit, which was the per-repo ceiling that used to bite before 250 GB. Files are content-addressed and deduplicated across history, so a repo of distinct chunks stores each chunk once.
record.limits_note: 250 GB per repository (soft - pack-file limit errors before it); 5 GB per push (LFS pushes exempt); individual files ~100 MB without LFS; path length 32,766 chars; rate limits 200 TSTU per 5-min window; anonymous access to public projects is being removed (new public projects blocked April 2026, all converted to private and anonymous disabled in 2027) - authenticate with a PAT.
record.reliability_note: Reliable but slow as bulk storage: no random-access read, no partial download, whole-repo clone semantics; the 'temporarily unavailable while repository is updated' pack-optimization window can block writes for large repos.

Inside one tenant the ceiling is much higher than the pool in principle - 2,000,000 site collections per org at up to 25 TB per site - but the 100 TB pool is the binding limit. Add unlimited free A1 user licenses (which add 0 GB but give each user a 100 GB or 1 TB OneDrive ceiling), and paid A3/A5 at 50/100 GB per license. Multiply across tenants for archival shards.

Tenant goes read-only when over pool.
record.reliability_note: Storage is enforced at the tenant pool level and tenants get flipped to read-only on overage - data survives but writes fail; per-user OneDrive caps were cut (5 TB -> 100 GB for A1) in 2024 with no migration path.
